overview: Black answers 1.f4 with 1...h6 and 2...g5, challenging the f4 pawn at once. After 3.fxg5 hxg5 4.Nxg5 White has won a pawn and Black gets the open h-file against h2 for a rook; Black relies on development and the file rather than material. White has the extra pawn and a sound game if it avoids the early tricks.

white_ideas.idea: Take the pawn with fxg5 and Nxg5, then consolidate with d4 and e4
Cover h2 and return material only if needed

black_ideas.idea: Use the half-open h-file with ...Rh8 and ...Bg7

typical_structures.structure: Open h-file after hxg5 with Black pawn down

character.notes: Early pawn offer and an open file produce unbalanced play where one side is a pawn down.

gambit.notes: Black allows 3.fxg5 hxg5 4.Nxg5 and does not get the pawn back by force; White can keep it.

soundness.notes: White simply takes the pawn; most players consider the Black idea dubious, with little more than the h-file.

structure.notes: The h-file is half-open for Black and the centre is fluid.

approach.notes: A rare reply to the Bird; strong players hardly use it.

level.notes: Dubious, so not for beginners, but ideas are simple; I would not call it Advanced.

sublines_that_differ.name: White declines
sublines_that_differ.how: No capture, the position stays tense and no material changes hands.

character.reason: Black plays on the h-file at the cost of a pawn, with early forcing exchanges.

gambit.reason: Black offers the g-pawn and White can keep the pawn after fxg5 hxg5 Nxg5.

soundness.reason: The pawn is hard to justify with only the h-file for compensation.

structure.reason: The h-file opens for Black while the centre is not yet fixed.

approach.reason: Few strong players answer the Bird this way.

level.reason: It is Dubious so never Beginner, and the ideas are not deep.

plans.reason: Black aims to use the open h-file and quick development against the White king side.
